title: Close the security completeness ratchet and wire the final gate
description:
Objective: flip the declared-boundary roster from "matches the source" to "every declared boundary has hostile coverage", so DoD 1 of the Security fault matrix (task-05ce9b8f982f448a9cdaa4142a653f32) becomes a mechanically checked fact rather than a claim. FINAL slice of the SPIDR re-slice.

HARD DEPENDENCIES — all five must be DONE, and re-measured on disk rather than trusted by status:
- task-9aca4b0524a648f1841237b40d4e345b — roster and harness
- task-aa32fdf7e5ea4fb7916d3d52e83cebf2 — transport
- task-924c5d82619f4dccb049636ed7a3f6f4 — integrity
- task-f643b972a9014c6aa0bf1257dc1892ef — durable store
- task-2259196ec7d84d699d1bd32f8556d6b4 — runtime/provider
- task-c994bd0a59f0472da5b106916aa27b37 — scheduler/activation

Deliverable, three parts:
1. CLOSE THE RATCHET. The roster currently asserts only that its 85 hand-written entries match a live source scan. This task adds the coverage assertion: every roster entry resolves to at least one BEFORE, one AFTER and one RACE case in the sibling slices, and the union of the five axis subsets equals the full 85-member set with no overlap and no gap. A boundary added to the source later, with no coverage, must redden here — that is what stops DoD 1 decaying silently after this epic closes.
2. WIRE THE FINAL GATE. `pnpm test:security` and `pnpm test:fault` both run as this task's gate. Read the OUTPUT of each, separately, with its own exit code — never `;`-chained, never piped into tail.
3. RECONCILE WITH tests/fault. `tests/fault/**` has its own owners (tests/fault/disaster-restore/** is task-0c89476b78044024b07c86c0c8986bd0; foundation/ and cross-host/ have theirs). This task does NOT write fault coverage — it records which parent DoD clauses the fault lane already satisfies and which remain, so the parent's completion is honest about the split rather than implying this slice set covered everything.

NOT in scope: adding hostile coverage for any boundary (that belongs to the axis slices — if one is missing coverage, reject it back rather than filling the gap here), corpus bytes, campaign scoring, claim decisions, or editing tests/fault/**.

Owned paths: tests/security/completeness.security.ts, plus the coverage-assertion additions to tests/security/boundary-roster.security.ts.

Verification: `pnpm test:security` and `pnpm test:fault`, each with its own captured exit code and a printed Test Files/Tests count line.
definitionOfDone: Every one of the 85 roster entries resolves to at least one BEFORE, one AFTER and one RACE case across the sibling slices; the assertion names any uncovered boundary by constant name and declaring file, not merely a count.
The union of the five axis subsets is asserted EQUAL to the full 85-member roster — both directions — with no boundary claimed by two axes and none claimed by zero.
A boundary constant ADDED to production source with no roster entry and no coverage turns a NAMED test red; a drill proves it, so the ratchet cannot decay silently after this epic closes.
Removing one axis slice's coverage for a single boundary turns a NAMED test red identifying that exact boundary — proving the coverage resolution reads real cases rather than a static list.

`pnpm test:security` and `pnpm test:fault` each run with their own captured exit code, neither `;`-chained nor piped, and each prints a Test Files/Tests count line; any foreign red is quoted verbatim and attributed by the path-attributed baseline rather than repaired.

The completion records, clause by clause, which of the parent task-05ce9b8f DoD items this slice set satisfies and which remain owned by tests/fault/** owners — so the parent closes on measured coverage, never on an implied one.
taskRails: Do NOT fill a coverage gap here. If an axis slice left a boundary uncovered, that slice is incomplete — report it rather than absorbing the work, or the ratchet ends up policing coverage this task wrote itself.
The roster stays hand-written and source-compared in both directions. A generated table cannot police its own generator.
Do not edit tests/fault/** — it has other owners. This task only RECORDS what the fault lane already covers.
Preserve foreign work; commit only the explicit owned paths by pathspec.

FINDING, reported not absorbed: runtime-provider is not missing coverage — its own slices assert `assertSweepsExactly` + `assertPositiveCounts` over all 24 boundaries x 3 arms — it is missing an IMPORTABLE coverage surface. implementationPlan.description: RED first. Create tests/security/completeness.security.ts with the whole-roster assertions failing before the normaliser exists. Four properties, each naming offenders rather than counting them, because DoD 1 and DoD 4 both require the failure to identify the exact boundary. (1) COVERAGE: every roster entry resolves to at least one BEFORE, one AFTER and one RACE case; the failure message lists each uncovered boundary as `constant (declaring file)` from the roster entry's own `file` field, not a bare count. (2) UNION EQUALS ROSTER, both directions: the union of the five axis subsets equals the full roster set -- assert roster-minus-union is empty AND union-minus-roster is empty, as two separate assertions with separate messages, because one direction catches a gap and the other catches a boundary claimed by an axis that does not roster it. (3) NO OVERLAP: no constant appears in two axis subsets; name any that does. (4) NO ZERO-CLAIM: every roster entry is claimed by exactly one axis subset. Derive the expected total from BOUNDARY_ROSTER.length and assert the five subset sizes sum to it, so the count is a consequence rather than a literal. Assert the resolved case count is positive before asserting any set property -- a silently-empty normalisation makes every set assertion pass vacuously, which is the same trap the integrity slice already guards at its :105.
implementationPlan.note:
RED FIRST, and it is red for the right reason. Created tests/security/completeness.security.ts (130 lines) carrying all six assertions with the per-axis resolver stubbed to `Object.freeze([])`.

The ONE pass is "parses a positive number of roster rows" — deliberate, and it is the evidence the roster regex is not silently matching zero. Everything downstream fails on the vacuity guard `expect(ALL_PAIRS.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)`, which is exactly the trap the integrity slice guards at its :105: with an empty normalisation every set assertion would otherwise pass, and the gate would ship green while proving nothing. The seventh failure is "resolves a positive case count on every axis", which names the axes that resolved nothing rather than counting them.

ASSERTIONS WRITTEN, all naming offenders rather than counting (DoD 1 and DoD 4 both require the failure to identify the exact boundary):
1. COVERAGE — every roster row resolves >=1 BEFORE, >=1 AFTER, >=1 RACE; each miss is reported as "CONSTANT (declaring/file.ts) has no BEFORE case", the file read from the roster row's own `file` field.
2. UNION EQUALS ROSTER, two SEPARATE `it`s with separate messages: "roster minus union is empty" (catches a gap) and "union minus roster is empty" (catches an axis covering something it does not roster).

4. NO ZERO-CLAIM, strengthened past the plan's ask: "claims every roster entry on exactly the axis the roster TAGS it with", so a boundary covered by the wrong axis reddens too, reported as "NAME (file) rostered transport, covered by integrity".

Every set assertion carries the positive-count guard as its FIRST line, so none of them can go vacuous later.

implementationPlan.description: GREEN the normaliser, inside tests/security/completeness.security.ts. It must read REAL CASE ENTRIES from the five axes' case tables -- import the case-table modules (the data), never the sibling `*.security.ts` test files -- and reduce them to one `Map<constant, Set<arm>>`. Handle the shape differences from step 1 explicitly: for the field-carrying tables take `entry.arm`; for the scheduler axis merge its three tables and map its RACES list to the RACE arm; for durable-store derive the arm from WHICH export the case came from (hostileBeforeCases -> BEFORE, hostileAfterCases -> AFTER, hostileRaceCases -> RACE) since those entries carry no arm field. THE RULE THAT MAKES DoD 4 SATISFIABLE: never write a literal list of covered constants anywhere in this file. Every membership answer must come from reducing an imported case table, so deleting one axis's coverage for one boundary changes the computed map and reddens a named test. A static list would agree with itself forever and is exactly the "generated table cannot police its own generator" failure the task rails name. If an axis exposes no importable table and only resolves coverage inside its own test file, STOP and report that as a finding -- it is a gap in that axis slice, not something to work around by re-deriving its cases here.
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN. tests/security/completeness.security.ts is 271 lines (37 of them the header rationale). `npx tsc -p tests/security/tsconfig.json` TSC_EXIT=0. `npx vitest run --config tests/security/vitest.config.ts completeness` EXIT=0, "Test Files 1 passed (1)", "Tests 8 passed (8)". Full lane `pnpm test:security` EXIT=0, "Test Files 10 passed (10)", "Tests 495 passed (495)" — exactly +1 file and +8 tests over the 9/487 baseline, which is the evidence no sibling suite got re-registered by my imports.

THE NORMALISER reduces five differently-shaped sources to one `Map<constant, Set<Arm>>` plus a parallel `Map<constant, Set<axis>>`. Four axes are read from IMPORTED DATA MODULES; no sibling `*.security.ts` is imported.
- transport: TRANSPORT_HOSTILE_CASES -> [entry.boundary, entry.arm].
- integrity: INTEGRITY_HOSTILE_CASES -> [entry.constant, entry.arm].
- durable-store: [...hostileBeforeCases, ...hostileAfterCases] -> [entry.boundary, entry.PHASE], plus hostileRaceCases -> RACE. STRONGER THAN THE PLAN ASKED: the plan said derive the arm from WHICH export the case came from, but RefusalCase actually carries a `phase` field, so reading it means a case filed under the wrong export resolves to the arm it declares rather than to the arm its filing implies. Only RaceCase genuinely carries nothing, so only RACE is implied.
- scheduler-activation: SIX tables, not the three the plan named — ACTIVATION_ADMISSION_CASES/EXPANSION_SUPERSESSION_CASES/SCHEDULER_DECISION_CASES carry `arm`, and ACTIVATION_ADMISSION_RACES/EXPANSION_SUPERSESSION_RACES/SCHEDULER_DECISION_RACES carry none and map to RACE.

THE FIFTH AXIS IS SCANNED, and step 1's finding is why. runtime-provider exposes NO importable case table: its `*-cases.ts` modules export `describe*(ledger, spec)` SUITE BUILDERS, and coverage lands in an in-memory Ledger during execution that `pool: "forks"` + `isolate: true` cannot carry across a file. `RUNTIME_PROVIDER_PARTITION` is 24 names with no arms — using it would be exactly the static list the rails forbid. I did NOT re-derive its cases and did NOT fill anything: the resolver reads the axis's own committed bytes for its LEDGER WRITE SITES, which is real evidence (delete a case, delete its write site) and is the same source-text technique every axis slice already uses to read the roster. Three regexes over `runtime-provider-*.security.ts` and `runtime-provider-*-cases.ts` only, so the ledger's own definition body and platform-fixtures' `refusedObservation` helper body cannot be miscounted as cases: ANCHOR (`const boundary|BOUNDARY = "X"`, and the object-property spec form `boundary: "X"`), ARM_SITE (`boundary, "BEFORE"|"AFTER"|"RACE"` — covers refused/refusedExactly/refusedWithoutLayer/refusedByManifestLayer, single-line or wrapped), RACE_SITE (`refusedSide`/`refusedObservation`, which push RACE without naming it). Each arm site attaches to the nearest PRECEDING anchor in its own file; a file holding arms but no anchor (only `runtime-provider-render-cases.ts`, which destructures `spec.boundary`) delegates them to every spec anchor, so deleting an arm there reddens both CLAUDE_RENDER_LAYERS and CODEX_RENDER_LAYERS.

NO LITERAL LIST AND NO LITERAL COUNT. `grep -n '93' completeness.security.ts` finds nothing; `AXES` is derived from the parsed roster rows rather than enumerated, so a sixth axis would surface as an unresolved axis instead of being silently dropped. The 8 passes therefore prove, without any hand-written help: the five subsets sum to the roster's 93 distinct constants, every one of the 93 resolves BEFORE+AFTER+RACE, union equals roster in both directions, and each constant is covered by exactly the axis the roster tags it with — which is what pins runtime-provider's 24 to runtime-provider rather than letting another axis's over-broad scan absorb them.

REPORTED, NOT ABSORBED, for the runtime-provider axis owner: exporting a `readonly {boundary, arm}[]` table from that axis would let `runtimeProviderPairs` (about 40 lines) be deleted outright and would make this axis as cheap to police as the other four.

implementationPlan.description: Mutation drills, two, and they are DoD items 3 and 4 rather than optional hardening. DRILL A (the ratchet cannot decay): add a new `*_LAYER` / `*_LAYERS` boundary constant to a production source with NO roster entry and NO coverage; a NAMED test must go red identifying it. This is the whole point of the task -- it proves a boundary added after this epic closes cannot slip in silently. Note the sibling fact recorded on this board: a new layer constant already reddens `pnpm test:security` and that suite runs in no other gate, so this drill is exercising a live ratchet, not a hypothetical one. Restore the production source EXACTLY -- it is not an owned path, so leaving a byte behind is a foreign-file edit. DRILL B (coverage resolution reads real cases): remove ONE axis's coverage for a single boundary -- delete or rename one case entry in that axis's table -- and confirm a NAMED test reddens identifying THAT boundary by name. If it reddens with a count or a generic message, the assertion is not naming offenders and step 2 must be strengthened. If it stays green, the normaliser is reading a static list and step 3 must be rewritten. Record for each drill the command, the failing test NAME and the exact assertion. Restore by re-editing, never `git checkout`, and confirm with `git diff --numstat` showing 0 added and 0 deleted across the touched files. One drill at a time.
